# FlipperForce Public API • Version 1

## How do I request an API key?

1. [Request a Public API key.](https://tools.flipperforce.com/integrations)
2. Use the API key as an Authorization HTTP header with Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer token-goes-here`

## Support / Help

* Email: support@flipperforce.com
* Chat: https://tools.flipperforce.com/

## Rate Limits

If you encounter a `429 Too Many Requests` response, you have submitted too many
requests in a short amount of time. Please decrease the amount or frequency of
your requests and try again.

## Changelog

### July 25, 2026 - v0.0.10

* Add support for [Activity Log](/operations/v1.workspace.activity-log.list).

### July 23, 2026 - v0.0.9

* Response format of `created_at` and `updated_at` fields now include microseconds. Old format: `2026-06-14T15:30:45Z` and new format: `2026-06-14T15:30:45.123456Z`

### July 21, 2026 - v0.0.8

* OpenAPI spec documents Bearer Token authentication strategy

### June 22, 2026 - v0.0.6

* Add support for [Project Income](/operations/v1.project.income.list).
* [Create Upload Intent](/operations/v1.workspace.upload-intent.create) properly documents API response code as 201 Created instead of 200 OK.

### June 21, 2026 - v0.0.4

* Add support for [Project Expenses: Transactions](/operations/v1.project.expense-transactions.list).
* Add support for [Project Expenses: Line Items](/operations/v1.project.expense-line-items.list).

### June 4, 2026 - v0.0.3

* Add support for [Project Expenses: Categories](/operations/v1.project.expense-categories.list).

### June 2, 2026 - v0.0.2

* Add support for [Expense Accounts](/operations/v1.workspace.expense-accounts.list).
* Add support for [Companies](/operations/v1.workspace.companies.list).
* Add support for [Company Categories](/operations/v1.workspace.companies.categories.list).

### September 3, 2025 - v0.0.1

* [Project Photo Log: Photos - Create](/operations/v1.project.photo-log.create) added support for ordering Photos by EXIF timestamp via parameter `photo_timestamp`.

### August 13, 2025

* [Create Upload Intent API](/operations/v1.workspace.upload-intent.create) now requires a new POST parameter `upload_type` noting the uploaded file's use case.

get.description:
Activity Log is a record of what actions have been performed within a Workspace by its Users. This is the best way to discover recent activity that has occurred in a Workspace.

While not every action in the software is logged here, it includes important activity across most software tools.

Results use cursor-based pagination and are ordered by `performed_at` with the most recent displaying first. Use `links.next` to fetch the next page of results.

The total number of records matching the search filter parameters is returned in `meta.total_count` and is useful for reporting purposes.

## Search Filters

Use the [Activity Log filters endpoint](/operations/v1.workspace.activity-log.filters) to discover Projects, Users and Activity Types usable as filter values.

Submit filters as query string parameters:

* performed_at
* project_uuids
* user_uuids
* activity_types

Filters are additive and are applied using AND semantics:

```text
(filter1 AND filter2 AND ...)
```

Filter values `project_uuids`, `user_uuids`, and `activity_types` use OR semantics:

```text
(
    project_uuids IN (...)
    AND user_uuids IN (...)
    AND activity_types IN (...)
)
```

## Search Filters - performed_at for querying by time

`performed_at` format follows RFC 3339 using second precision and a timezone. For example, for example `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z`.

Times in UTC timezone end in `Z`. Specify timezones by using UTC offsets such as `2026-05-31T19:00:00-04:00` for Eastern Daylight Time.

Each timestamp requires a timezone.

Search values are normalized to UTC and results are returned as UTC.

## Example: Filter by multiple Projects and Activity Types

`project_uuids[]` and `activity_types[]` filters support finding multiple values. Like `(project1 OR project2) AND (type1 OR type2)`.

You can find logs associated with multiple Project when the Activity Type is either `project.created` or `project.stage.updated`.

```text
GET /api/v1/workspace/{workspace}/activity-log/list?project_uuids[]=9d0e1f23-4567-489a-bcde-f0123456789a&project_uuids[]=dff54a48-2113-44c5-be0c-a3a9f84c25e7&activity_types[]=project.created&activity_types[]=project.stage.updated
```

## Example: Find activity performed at or after July 1, 2026 at 12:00 a.m. EDT

Set an inclusive lower bound using `performed_at[gte]` (greater-than or equal to). `-04:00` is the timezone offset for Eastern Daylight Time:

```text
GET /api/v1/workspace/{workspace}/activity-log/list?performed_at[gte]=2026-07-01T00:00:00-04:00
```

## Example: Find activity performed before July 1, 2026 at 12:00 a.m. EDT

Set an exclusive upper bound using `performed_at[lt]` (less-than). `-04:00` is the timezone offset for Eastern Daylight Time:

```text
GET /api/v1/workspace/{workspace}/activity-log/list?performed_at[lt]=2026-07-01T00:00:00-04:00
```

## Example: Find activity performed in July 2026 (EDT)

Set a lower bound (`performed_at[gte]`) and upper bound (`performed_at[lt]`) to find activity within a single month. Notice the upper bound (exclusive) is next month August 1 at 12:00am:

```text
GET /api/v1/workspace/{workspace}/activity-log/list?performed_at[gte]=2026-07-01T00:00:00-04:00&performed_at[lt]=2026-08-01T00:00:00-04:00
```

Create a new Project by providing its address.

### Automatically Find Property Data

Your [FlipperForce Subscription](https://tools.flipperforce.com/billing) includes access to nationwide data on over 150+
million properties across the United States. [See examples of this data.](https://www.flipperforce.com/software-features/property-data)

Pass the flag `fetch_property_data: true` to automatically search for
Property Specs, Owner Information, Property History, Sales History and
more using this Project's address.

Fetching property data will increase API call processing time. If you are
creating many Projects, omit this flag to maximize throughput without
searching for property data.

### Project Pipeline Stage

Use the `stage` property to specify the Pipeline Stage. This controls
where in your Project workflow the new Project will begin.

If you omit this property the Project will begin in the "New Lead" stage.

post.description:
Create an Expense Transaction with Line Items to track your expenses. Associate them with a [Company](/operations/v1.workspace.companies.list), [Expense Category](/operations/v1.project.expense-categories.list) and [Expense Account](/operations/v1.workspace.expense-accounts.list) to then use reporting features.

Expenses are visible in the web application user interface in the Project Expense Tracker tool.

## Reporting on Transactions and Expenses

A Transaction has many Expense Line Items. Use the [Project Expenses: Line Items API](/operations/v1.project.expense-line-items.list) for reporting purposes like:

* Year-to-Date Totals
* Per Company Totals
* Per Expense Category Totals
* Per Expense Account Totals

## Understanding FlipperForce expense tracking concepts

Think of each Expense Transaction as starting from the receipt/invoice you receive from a vendor, or as each charge on a credit card statement.

Each purchase or payment is stored as an Expense Transaction. And each item or service purchased on that transaction (like items on a receipt) is stored as an Expense Line Item on that Expense Transaction.

FlipperForce allows you to go beyond simple accounting by tracking each Expense Line Item in an Expense Category, so you can compare your Budget vs Actuals spending for each category.

## Setup 1: Workspace Companies

The [Companies API](/operations/v1.workspace.companies.list) is for tracking each vendor you do business with. For example, The Home Depot where you purchase materials, or your most reliable general contractor who invoices you for completed jobs.

Companies are shared across all Projects in your Workspace, so you can track your spending with every vendor across every Project.

Create a Company record for each vendor you make purchases from.

## Setup 2: Workspace Expense Accounts

The [Expense Accounts API](/operations/v1.workspace.expense-accounts.list) is for tracking each credit card, bank account, Venmo/PayPal account, or payment method used to pay for expenses.

Expense Accounts are shared across all Projects in your Workspace, so you can track your spending for every Account.

Create an Expense Account record for each account your business makes purchases from.

## Setup 3: Project Expense Categories

The [Project Expenses: Categories API](/operations/v1.project.expense-categories.list) is for categorizing your spending for each Expense Line Item. For example, Interior Doors, Kitchen, or Appliances.

**NOTE:** Each Project has a separate list of Expense Categories. You must use the Expense Category associated with the Project where you are creating expenses.

Project Expense Categories must be added from the Project's Deal Analysis - Repair Estimator tool. For example, within the "Exteriors" top-level category, create a new category called "Roofing" to track expenses like shingles, nails, underlayment, etc.

The fastest way to create repair categories (and thus expense categories) is by loading a Repair Estimator Template onto the Project.

## Example: Creating an Expense Transaction with a Receipt

With setup complete, you can now create your first Expense Transaction.

Let's use an example purchase from The Home Depot. Assume you received a receipt that has the following data:

* Company: The Home Depot
* Date: 06/13/26
* Items:
    * 1/2 in. x 4 ft. x 8 ft. Plywood Sheet - $28.45
    * Deck Screws, 1 lb. Box - $9.97
    * 1 Gal. Interior Eggshell Paint - $29.98
    * 20V Cordless Drill - $42.67
* Subtotal: $111.07
* Sales Tax (8.45%): $9.38
* Grand Total: $120.45
* Chip Read XXXXXXXXXXX4213 VISA

### Step 1: Upload the Receipt (optional)

Follow the documentation in the [Project Receipts: Create API](/operations/v1.project.receipts.create) for uploading your Receipt file.

Uploading a Receipt is optional. You can also attach it later by updating the Expense Transaction.

The rest of the example will assume you received an HTTP Response that has the uploaded Receipt's `uuid`, which can be associated with the Transaction below.

### Step 2: Find The Home Depot in your list of Companies

Use the [Companies API](/operations/v1.workspace.companies.list) to find all Companies in your Workspace and locate the `uuid` of The Home Depot in your Workspace.

### Step 3: Find Visa 4213 credit card in your list of Expense Accounts

Use the [Expense Accounts: List API](/operations/v1.workspace.expense-accounts.list) to find the `uuid` of your Visa credit card with card number 4213.

### Step 4: Find relevant Expense Categories for each item

Use the [Project Expenses: Categories: List API](/operations/v1.project.expense-categories.list) to find the `uuid` of the Expense Categories relevant to each item you purchased.

The example Home Depot line items could be the following:

* 1/2 in. x 4 ft. x 8 ft. Plywood Sheet - "Framing"
* Deck Screws, 1 lb. Box - "Decks/Porches"
* 1 Gal. Interior Eggshell Paint - "Bathrooms"
* 20V Cordless Drill - "Tools"

### Step 5: Create the Expense Transaction

The following example request associates the Company (The Home Depot), Expense Account (Visa 4213), Expense Categories, and Receipt from the previous instructions.

Submit each purchased item as the `expenses` array.

## How taxes are handled

Most receipts do not explicitly list how much tax was incurred for each item. But a receipt only lists the total tax charged as a percentage of the subtotal.

FlipperForce automatically distributes the Total Tax across each line item amount.

This allows you to account for spending on taxes as part of your total construction costs.

Read the following example transaction for how taxes are distributed:

```monospace
Nails          $100
Decking        $300
Shingles       $600

     Subtotal $1000
    Total Tax  $100

  Grand Total $1100
```

FlipperForce will automatically distribute the Total Tax across each Expense Line Item when you save the Transaction:

```monospace
Item          |     Amount |   Tax | Total
--------------+------------+-------+-------
Nails         |       $100 |   $10 |  $110
Decking       |       $300 |   $30 |  $330
Shingles      |       $600 |   $60 |  $660
```

The Tax across all items still totals $100 (which was entered as Total Tax), and the Transaction Grand Total is computed as 110 + 330 + 660 = 1100.

## Default fields from the root level

Some fields submitted at the root level will be automatically applied to each item in the `expenses` array when omitted from the expense item.

* `date`
* `invoice_number`
* `company_uuid`
* `expense_account_uuid`
* `expense_category_uuid`

Here is an example using the `date` field and overwriting it:

```json
{
  "date": "2026-06-13",
  "expenses": [
    {
      // Unnecessary because the root level uses "date"
      "date": "2026-06-13",
    },
    {
      // But can be submitted with a different "date"
      // to override the root level value
      "date": "2026-07-25",
    },
  ]
}
```

get.description:
List Expense line items within a Project.

Expense Line Items are the individual charges within an Expense Transaction, such as the items purchased and listed on a receipt.

## Reporting on Total Amounts

See the `data.totals` property in the response for the sum total of various Expense Line Item fields (before pagination).

* `data.totals.amount` - Sum of all `amount` values for all matching Expenses (excludes tax)
* `data.totals.tax` - Sum of all `tax` values for all matching Expenses
* `data.totals.total` - Sum of all `total` values for all matching Expenses (amount + tax)

The total number of records matching the query parameters is in `meta.total_count`.

## Filter by date range

 Supports limiting to date ranges by using a combination of these operators:

 * date[gt] - greater than
 * date[gte] - greater than or equal to
 * date[lt] - less than
 * date[lte] - less than or equal to

List Income records within a Project.

Income is visible in the web application user interface in the Project Income Tracker tool.

## Reporting on Total Amounts

See the `data.totals` property in the response for the sum total of Income before pagination.

* `data.totals.amount` - Sum of all `amount` values for all matching Income records

The total number of records matching the query parameters is in `meta.total_count`.

## Filter by date range

Supports limiting to date ranges by using a combination of these operators:

* date[gt] - greater than
* date[gte] - greater than or equal to
* date[lt] - less than
* date[lte] - less than or equal to

## Example: Year-to-Date Income

Request using a year-to-date range, then read the returned totals.

For example, Income year-to-date through June 19, 2026.

* date[gte]=2026-01-01
* date[lte]=2026-06-19

```text
GET /api/v1/project/{projectV1}/income/list?date[gte]=2026-01-01&date[lte]=2026-06-19
```

## Example: Rental Income

```text
GET /api/v1/project/{projectV1}/income/list?types[]=rental
```

post.description:
Creating an Upload Intent is Step 1 in uploading files.

Submit metadata about the file you intend to upload. The Response
includes a Signed URL, HTTP Method, and HTTP Headers where your client
will be temporarily authorized to upload the file. Use the Response data
to construct a file upload request in Step 2.

Step 2 is using the Signed URL, Method, and Headers from Step 1 to upload
the file to file storage:

```
x-amz-acl: private
Content-MD5: rz1TrXzmoB4WmdeUde+CIQ==
Content-Type: image/png
... above are example headers from an Upload Intent ...
POST https://the-signed-url-here
raw-binary-file-data-here
```

Step 3 after uploading succeeds is to call the next API for the specific
use case you uploaded the file. Each use case has its own API call where
you must supply the `uuid` returned in Step 1, allowing Step 3 to find
and reference the uploaded file:

* [Create a Project Receipt](/operations/v1.project.receipts.create)
* [Create a Photo Log Photo](/operations/v1.project.photo-log.create)
* [Create a Project Update Photo](/operations/v1.project.updates.photos.create)

### Response from Signed URL: Response Codes

| Code | Description |
| - | - |
| 200 OK        | File successfully received and satisfied all validation checks. No body content. |
| 400 Bad Request | Perhaps the uploaded file's MD5 checksum did not match what was given in the Upload Intent. Retry by requesting a new Upload Intent and signed URL. |
| 403 Forbidden | The signed URL has expired. Retry by request a new Upload Intent and signed URL. |

### Response from Signed URL

The Signed URL response defaults to returning XML. If you want JSON,
submit a header `Accept: application/json`.

Example Error Response Body when the Content-MD5 header does not match
what was submitted in the Request Body:

```
{
  "Code": "BadDigest",
  "Message": "",
  "BucketName": "flipperforce-prod",
  "RequestId": "tx000007027848ea442f7f9-006839cfe7-1060947b4-nyc3c",
  "HostId": "1060947b4-nyc3c-nyc3-zg03"
}
```

(Required) Specify how you intend to use the uploaded file.
The metadata submitted will be used to validate the file type
can be used for this use case. Accepted values:

* `photo-log-photo` - [Project Photo Log: Photo](/operations/v1.project.photo-log.create)
* `project-update-photo` - [Project Update: Photo](/operations/v1.project.updates.photos.create)

project_stages.description:
Projects within a Workspace can be assigned to one of these
Project Stage keys. Keys are the machine-readable values
accepted by the API. Values are the human-readable text for
that Stage. A Project's current Stage is returned via the
Project schema as field `stage`.

Workspace Owners can customize the human-readable values using
the web application, but the machine-readable values cannot be
changed. For example, if the human-readable text for
`pending_purchase` was customized to be
"Evaluating Deal" then the API still requires submitting
`pending_purchase` to move the Project to the Evaluating Deal
Stage.
